setlist.title: Beat It On Down the Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Reviewer highlights Good Lovin' as one of the show's standout performances; Good Lovin' is described as a monster, with Pigpen delivering strong vocal rapping [11][13]
- **Loser** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Loser as especially strong [11]

## The recordings

- **gd71-04-10.sbd.willy.8674.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 147 min; rated 4.42/5 by 19 [1]. Said about its sound: Garcia's guitar begins to break up and distort on the tape during Truckin', though he plays some good licks; Reviewer finds the recording's balance imperfect, though the playing is virtuosic; Reviewer calls the recording extremely crisp [4][7][11][13]
- **gd1971-04-10.177902.sbd.blackwood.chastain.gravel.flac1644**: soundboard; 19 songs; 148 min [2]

## Around the show

- A bomb scare reportedly emptied the hall; people were let back in, and the crowd seemed larger afterward [7]
- Band ran well over its allotted time; the student organizer said they were consequently banned from returning to F&M [7]
- Venue was a small auditorium that might once have been a church, with two large double doors [8]
- Philadelphia-area fans bought extra tickets so out-of-town Deadheads could attend [8]
- The show fell on the night before Easter, with the New Riders opening [9]
- Tickets cost three dollars each, and the band's PA system was tie-dyed [9]
- Reviewer drove down from Goddard in northern Vermont, where heavy snow had fallen since Thanksgiving [14]
- As doors opened, the New Riders were warming up with Jerry playing pedal steel [14]
- This show is less well known than the Port Chester run, and shows newer songs in rotation [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-04-10.sbd.willy.8674.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Willy and Mark Pfortmiller; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1971-04-10.177902.sbd.blackwood.chastain.gravel.flac1644**: taped by Anon; transferred by Mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, Track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Vault master reel sourced files [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Franklin & Marshall College - Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1971/artwork/franklin-marshall-college-poster-0) [16]
